title: Every PPT channel has finite entanglement-breaking index
abstract: We prove that every PPT linear map has finite entanglement-breaking index, thereby establishing the eventual entanglement-breaking property of PPT channels in full generality. Furthermore, by utilizing completely positive maps with low entanglement dimensionality, we show that a large family of PPT maps, which strictly containing the class of 2-superpositive maps, has entanglement-breaking index bounded above by 3, uniformly in the dimension. In particular, these results provide strong evidence that the PPT-cubed conjecture may hold in full generality.

bite.hook: Every PPT quantum channel is proven to eventually break entanglement, with a broad class doing so in at most 3 steps.
tldr: Proved that all positive partial transpose (PPT) linear maps have a finite entanglement-breaking index.
Showed a large family of PPT maps strictly containing 2-superpositive maps has an index bounded above by 3.
Provided strong theoretical support that the long-standing PPT-cubed conjecture holds in full generality.
bite.whyItMatters: Understanding when repeated noise completely destroys quantum entanglement is fundamental to setting theoretical limits on quantum communication and long-distance quantum networks.
bite.eli5: Entanglement links particles in a delicate quantum relationship. This proof shows that running signals through a specific, well-behaved type of noisy channel will always break that quantum link completely after a finite number of repeats—often in just three rounds.
